facts.raw_span: A 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
The patient was treated with 2 intravitreal anti–vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections
her macular edema was completely resolved, without recurrence
No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case
At 6 months: No abnormality observed
At 12 months: En face OCT revealed hyperreflective tissues starting to proliferate on retinal vessels
At 12 months: OCTA B-scan showed pyramid-shaped proliferations
At 15 months: Hyperreflective tissues increased in size with angiogenic sprouts showing flow signals extending vertically
At 18 months: Development observed in area of preexisting proliferation
At 21 months: Enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface
Performed at 21 months showing dendritic vascular-like structures
Figure 1: Sequential development over 1 year showing progression from normal vessels to proliferation

The patient was treated with 2 intravitreal anti–vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections
her macular edema was completely resolved, without recurrence
No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case
At 6 months: No abnormality observed
At 12 months: En face OCT revealed hyperreflective tissues starting to proliferate on retinal vessels

concepts.why: The patient's OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues starting to proliferate on retinal vessels, and at 21 months, enlarged horizontal structures along the retina surface were observed, consistent with neovascularization.

The patient's OCTA B-scan at 12 months showed pyramid-shaped proliferations, and at 18 months, development was observed in the area of preexisting proliferation, consistent with retinal angiomatous proliferation.
The patient's OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues starting to proliferate on retinal vessels, consistent with type 1 neovascularization.
The patient's OCTA B-scan at 12 months showed pyramid-shaped proliferations, consistent with type 2 neovascularization.
The patient presented with macular edema, which was completely resolved after treatment with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections.
Although not explicitly mentioned, the patient's treatment with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections and the presence of macular edema could be related to diabetic retinopathy.
Although not explicitly mentioned, the patient's treatment with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections and the presence of macular edema could be related to hypertensive retinopathy.
The patient's age and the presence of macular edema and neovascularization are consistent with age-related macular degeneration.
